source.author: Islamic Economics
source.body_text: In 696 CE, Caliph Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan made a bold decision: replace the Byzantine and Persian coins circulating in Islamic lands with purely Islamic coinage. The gold dinar and silver dirham became the most trusted currencies of the medieval world. Discover how Al-Ghazali articulated the principle later known as Gresham's Law, and how Al-Maqrizi conducted one of history's first studies of inflation. Topics: Gold Dinar, Silver Dirham, Abd al-Malik, Al-Ghazali, Ibn Taymiyyah, Inflation Series: Historical Islamic Economics (Part I) • Episode 4 of 6

thread: Most people think currency is about economics. It's actually about sovereignty. Abd al-Malik replaced Byzantine and Persian coins with Islamic dinars in 696 CE.
The Islamic dinar and dirham became the most trusted currencies of the medieval world. Merchants from Baghdad to Cordoba accepted them without question.
Al-Ghazali understood what we now call Gresham's Law centuries before Gresham was born. Good money drives out bad money when governments interfere.

Al-Maqrizi conducted one of history's first systematic studies of inflation. He tracked how currency debasement destroyed purchasing power across generations. https://islamiceconomics.github.io/podcast.html#ep-4

linkedin.post: In 696 CE, Caliph Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan made a decision that would reshape medieval commerce: replace all Byzantine and Persian coins with purely Islamic currency. The resulting gold dinar and silver dirham became the most trusted currencies of their era. From Baghdad to Cordoba, merchants accepted them without hesitation. Centuries before European economists, Islamic scholars understood monetary principles we use today. Al-Ghazali articulated what we now call Gresham's Law. Al-Maqrizi conducted one of history's first systematic inflation studies, tracking how currency debasement destroyed purchasing power across generations. Currency was never just about economics. It was about sovereignty, trust, and the flow of civilizations. Listen: https://islamiceconomics.github.io/podcast.html#ep-4
